findings.issue_text: lib/validators/email_validator.rb:18 — BlockedEmail.should_block? uses case-sensitive lookup and the unique index is case-sensitive, so a blocked address like spam@x.com can be bypassed by signing up as SPAM@x.com; emails should be downcased before storage/lookup and the index made case-insensitive (e.g. lower(email) unique index)

app/models/blocked_email.rb:13-17 — should_block? performs a non-atomic read-modify-write (match_count += 1 then save), so concurrent signup attempts lose increments and last_match_at can become stale; should use an atomic update like update_all("match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...")

app/models/blocked_email.rb:13-17 — record.save's return value is ignored, so failed saves silently drop match statistics; more importantly, should_block? performs a DB write as a side effect inside an ActiveModel validation, making validation non-idempotent since every signup attempt (even ones failing other validations) mutates the blocked_emails table

app/models/user.rb:45-47 — validates :email, uniqueness: true remains case-sensitive (Rails default), allowing Foo@bar.com and foo@bar.com to both register; should use uniqueness: { case_sensitive: false } with normalized storage

spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb — spec only covers the BlockedEmail.should_block? path; no test coverage for the whitelist/blacklist domain logic moved out of User#email_validator into the new validator, so the refactor removed existing behavior coverage without porting the old email_in_restriction_setting? specs

app/controllers/users_controller.rb:194-199 — the new errors/values JSON payload the frontend depends on (result.errors.email, result.values.email) has no controller spec asserting the shape; if user.errors.to_hash keys or structure change, the client silently stops marking rejected emails

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:17 — rejectedEmails is never cleared and the controller is a long-lived modal singleton, so after a successful signup or modal close/reopen previously rejected emails stay in the array and a legitimately reusable address keeps showing 'invalid' with no reset except a page reload

app/models/blocked_email.rb:12 — should_block? runs a SELECT plus a full model save (with validations/callbacks) on every matching signup attempt, i.e. two queries plus callback overhead per attempt; an atomic single UPDATE ... WHERE email = ? would suffice, and attackers can trigger unbounded writes to the table by repeatedly submitting a blocked email (minor DoS/row-churn concern)

lib/validators/email_validator.rb:18 — the blocked check is skipped whenever any other email error is present (record.errors[attribute].blank?), so an email that is both format-invalid and blocked never records a match in statistics; additionally the blocked-specific I18n message gets mapped by the client to the generic user.email.invalid message, losing the blocked-specific reason
lib/validators/email_validator.rb:24 — file is missing a trailing newline, which will produce noise in future diffs; trivial but worth fixing in the same PR

goldens.comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.

The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/blocked_email.rb:13-17 — record.save's return value is ignored, so failed saves silently drop match statistics; more importantly, should_block? performs a DB write as a side effect inside an ActiveModel validation, making validation non-idempotent since every signup attempt (even ones failing other validations) mutates the blocked_emails table

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a side-effecting write inside `BlockedEmail.should_block?` (increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`, then `record.save`) and calls it from `EmailValidator#validate_each` (`lib/validators/email_validator.rb:12-15`), which is used as an ActiveModel validation on `User` (`app/models/user.rb:46-47`). That makes validations non-idempotent and can mutate `blocked_emails` even when the overall user creation later fails for other reasons. Also, `record.save`’s return value is ignored (`app/models/blocked_email.rb:13-17`), so failed saves silently lose the intended statistics update. This is a concrete, diff-grounded design/behavior concern, though not necessarily a functional defect in signup itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/user.rb:45-47 — validates :email, uniqueness: true remains case-sensitive (Rails default), allowing Foo@bar.com and foo@bar.com to both register; should use uniqueness: { case_sensitive: false } with normalized storage

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes User email validation to `validates :email, presence: true, uniqueness: true` (app/models/user.rb) without specifying `case_sensitive: false` or showing any normalization of `email`. Rails’ model-level uniqueness validator is case-sensitive by default, so the concern is grounded in the changed code, but whether it actually allows duplicate registrations depends on database collation/indexing and any normalization not shown in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb — spec only covers the BlockedEmail.should_block? path; no test coverage for the whitelist/blacklist domain logic moved out of User#email_validator into the new validator, so the refactor removed existing behavior coverage without porting the old email_in_restriction_setting? specs

adjudication.rationale: The diff moves the whitelist/blacklist domain restriction logic from `User#email_validator` into the new `lib/validators/email_validator.rb` (`SiteSetting.email_domains_whitelist` / `email_domains_blacklist` + `email_in_restriction_setting?`). However, the newly added spec `spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb` only asserts behavior for the `BlockedEmail.should_block?` branch and does not cover the whitelist/blacklist paths, leaving that refactored logic untested in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/users_controller.rb:194-199 — the new errors/values JSON payload the frontend depends on (result.errors.email, result.values.email) has no controller spec asserting the shape; if user.errors.to_hash keys or structure change, the client silently stops marking rejected emails

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes UsersController#create failure JSON to include `errors: user.errors.to_hash` and `values: user.attributes.slice("name", "username", "email")`, and the frontend now branches on `result.errors.email` and `result.values.email` to cache rejected emails. The diff adds model/validator specs but no controller/request spec asserting this response shape, so a future change to `user.errors.to_hash` structure/keys could break the client behavior without test coverage. This is a test/contract gap rather than a direct functional bug shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:17 — rejectedEmails is never cleared and the controller is a long-lived modal singleton, so after a successful signup or modal close/reopen previously rejected emails stay in the array and a legitimately reusable address keeps showing 'invalid' with no reset except a page reload

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` and appends to it on failed signup (`pushObject(result.values.email)`), and the `emailValidation` computed property short-circuits to `failed: true` when the current email is contained in that array. In the shown changes there is no code path that ever clears `rejectedEmails` (neither on success nor on subsequent modal uses), so this introduces persistent client-side state that can keep marking an email as invalid without re-checking. The claim about the controller being a long-lived singleton/modal lifecycle is not directly verifiable from the diff, but the lack of any reset is grounded in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/blocked_email.rb:12 — should_block? runs a SELECT plus a full model save (with validations/callbacks) on every matching signup attempt, i.e. two queries plus callback overhead per attempt; an atomic single UPDATE ... WHERE email = ? would suffice, and attackers can trigger unbounded writes to the table by repeatedly submitting a blocked email (minor DoS/row-churn concern)

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/blocked_email.rb, BlockedEmail.should_block? does `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` (a SELECT) and then mutates and `record.save` (an UPDATE plus validations/callbacks) on every matching attempt. This matches the finding about extra query/callback overhead; it could be reduced to a single atomic UPDATE (e.g., update_all with increment) and avoid full-model save. Also, because it increments match_count and updates last_match_at on every attempt, repeated submissions of a blocked email will cause unbounded write churn to that row (though not unbounded row growth). This is a performance/abuse-resistance concern rather than a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/validators/email_validator.rb:18 — the blocked check is skipped whenever any other email error is present (record.errors[attribute].blank?), so an email that is both format-invalid and blocked never records a match in statistics; additionally the blocked-specific I18n message gets mapped by the client to the generic user.email.invalid message, losing the blocked-specific reason

adjudication.rationale: In `EmailValidator#validate_each`, the blocked-email path is guarded by `record.errors[attribute].blank? and BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)`, so if any earlier validation adds an email error (e.g., whitelist/blacklist via `user.email.not_allowed`), `BlockedEmail.should_block?` is never called and `match_count/last_match_at` are not updated even when the email is in `blocked_emails`. Separately, the client stores failed emails in `rejectedEmails` and then always returns `I18n.t('user.email.invalid')` for them, discarding any server-provided blocked-specific message (`user.email.blocked`) returned via `users_controller#create` as `errors`.
